title: Conformance tests: shared fixtures + CI gates for SDK parity (auth/retry/timeout/streaming/errors)
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Goal
Ship a cross-language conformance test suite + shared fixtures and wire it into CI so redwood-sdk-python, redwood-sdk-typescript, and redwood-sdk-go must all pass the same behavioral checks for:
- Retry policy (retryable status codes + network errors, Retry-After handling, backoff/jitter, max attempts)
- Timeout model (connect/read/overall semantics; cancellation/abort behavior)
- Error taxonomy (typed/structured error fields; request_id propagation; retryable flag)
- Streaming semantics (disconnect handling, partial output behavior, cancellation, and retry guidance constraints)

Context / why
We keep seeing “works in TS but not in Python/Go” issues around retries, timeouts, and streaming disconnects (esp. behind proxies). This suite is the enforcement mechanism: once implemented, parity becomes hard to regress.

Non-goals
- End-to-end performance benchmarking.
- Golden model output correctness or prompt/evals.
- Testing new auth mechanisms beyond existing API keys/tokens (auth precedence is covered only insofar as it impacts request headers and error shapes).

Proposed approach
1) Shared fixture spec (language-agnostic)
- Define fixtures as declarative JSON/YAML cases (request + server behavior + expected client behavior).
- Each case includes:
  - Scenario name + category (retry/timeout/error/streaming)
  - Server script (sequence of responses / timing / disconnect point)
  - Expected client observations (attempt count bounds, backoff behavior constraints, error fields)
  - Invariants (e.g., must respect Retry-After >= X ms; must not retry non-retryable 4xx)

2) Local test server (“conformance harness”)
- Implement a lightweight HTTP server runnable in CI (Docker) that can:
  - Return 429 with Retry-After in both formats: seconds + HTTP-date
  - Return 500/502/503/504 with consistent error payload
  - Simulate network failures (connection reset, premature FIN) and slow responses (read timeout)
  - Provide a streaming endpoint that can:
    - Emit N chunks then disconnect
    - Stall mid-stream (no bytes) to trigger read timeout
    - Send a final error event (where applicable) vs abrupt disconnect
- The server must echo a stable request_id header and optionally include it in JSON error bodies to validate propagation.

3) Per-SDK adapters (thin)
- Each SDK repo includes a small adapter layer mapping:
  - How to configure retries/timeouts
  - How to invoke a standard request (chat/completions/stream)
  - How errors are captured and normalized for assertions
- All business logic stays in the SDK; the adapter should only be glue.

4) CI integration + gating
- Add GitHub Actions workflows in each SDK repo:
  - Spin up harness (Docker service)
  - Run conformance tests with deterministic settings (fixed jitter seed if supported)
  - Upload artifacts: logs, attempt timelines, failing fixture name(s)
- Make conformance a required check for merges to main.
- Add a nightly run against latest main to catch flaky behavior and environment-dependent issues.

Key acceptance criteria
- A single fixture change (e.g., update retry-after parsing expectations) fails all non-conforming SDKs in their respective CI.
- Coverage includes at minimum:
  Retry:
  - 429 w/ Retry-After seconds
  - 429 w/ Retry-After HTTP-date
  - 500/502/503/504 retryable
  - 400/401/403/404 NOT retryable
  - Network error retryable classification (connection reset / DNS failure where feasible)
  - Max attempts enforced and surfaced in error
  Timeout:
  - Overall timeout triggers and aborts request
  - Streaming read timeout triggers with partial output preserved (if any)
  - Cancellation/abort closes underlying connection and stops iteration
  Errors:
  - request_id present in error object on both streaming + non-streaming failures
  - retryable flag consistent with standard taxonomy
  Streaming:
  - Partial output semantics consistent (chunks yielded prior to disconnect)
  - Disconnect raises typed error with request_id + disconnect reason (best-effort)
  - No automatic retry of streaming requests by default (verify behavior)
- Flake rate < 1% on nightly (tracked over 7 days) with documented mitigations if higher.

Deliverables
- Shared fixture pack (versioned) and harness implementation.
- Documentation for adding new fixtures + running locally.
- CI workflows + required checks in each SDK repo.

Open questions
- Where does the “source of truth” live?
  Option A: separate repo (redwood-sdk-conformance) referenced as submodule/vendor.
  Option B: copy fixture pack into each repo and keep in sync (higher drift risk).
  Current leaning: separate repo OR a published artifact (tarball) pinned by version.
- Determinism for jitter/backoff: require SDKs to support injecting RNG seed for tests, or assert only bounds (min/max) rather than exact timings.
- Network failure simulation portability across CI runners (Linux only?). Might need to scope to connection resets + server close rather than true DNS failures.

Risks + mitigations
- Flaky timing-based assertions → assert bounds and event ordering; avoid wall-clock strictness; prefer monotonic timers.
- CI runtime bloat → parallelize fixtures; keep harness lightweight; run full suite on main/nightly and a smoke subset on PRs if needed.
- Streaming tests vary by HTTP stack → assert invariants (partial yields + typed error) rather than byte-for-byte framing.

References
- Confluence: Conformance test suite plan (fixtures + golden error shapes)
- Confluence: SDK retry/timeout standard (v1)
- ADRs: Retry policy v1; Timeout model
- Support drivers: 429 handling, streaming disconnects behind proxy

Related work
- Python: add conformance fixtures runner + CI integration (PR: redwood-sdk-python#857)
- Go: conformance harness integration (PR: redwood-sdk-go#635)
- TS: pending PR to wire harness into workflows (owner: Dana Lo)
comments: 2026-01-17 (Ibrahim Khan): We should avoid timing-exact backoff asserts; instead validate that attempts increase delay (monotonic) and that Retry-After is honored as a minimum. For jitter, we can optionally support an injected RNG/seed in each SDK, but I’d rather not block on it.

2026-01-22 (Dana Lo): TS side can stand up the harness as a docker service in GH actions. Biggest question is fetch streaming behavior in Node 18/20 and how to reliably simulate a mid-chunk disconnect. Suggest we assert: (a) partial tokens yielded, (b) stream throws a typed StreamDisconnectedError w/ request_id if available.

2026-01-25 (Mateusz Zielinski): Go net/http makes it straightforward to enforce context cancellation. For the harness, we can simulate slow read by pausing writes. We should include a fixture that stalls after first chunk to ensure read timeout triggers and stream iteration exits.

2026-01-29 (Sahana Iyer): CI plan proposal: run conformance suite as a required check on PRs but only “smoke” fixtures (429 + 500 + request_id propagation + one streaming disconnect). Full matrix runs on main + nightly. If smoke fails, we block merges; if nightly fails, page owners and track flake budget.

2026-02-03 (Allison Grant): Please ensure we capture attempt timeline logs as artifacts: attempt_number, computed_backoff_ms, retry_after_ms (if any), timeout_ms, request_id. That’s needed for debugging both CI and real customer behavior.

2026-02-10 (Marcus Lin): Reminder: the harness and fixtures must never include real secrets. If we test auth header presence, use a static dummy token and ensure SDK debug logs redact it; do not store any customer-like keys in fixtures.

2026-02-18 (Ibrahim Khan): Confirmed with platform team: request_id should always be present for non-streaming errors; streaming path is being improved but the conformance suite should accept best-effort on abrupt disconnects. We still require that the SDK error object includes request_id if it was observed in headers prior to disconnect.
activity: 2026-01-16: Ticket created by Talia Benson; scoped as P0 to unblock parity rollout gates.

2026-02-20: Go harness integration PR opened; TS adapter design in progress; next step is to finalize repo location/versioning for fixtures and make checks required.
